DecSummary: On September 2, 1944 the worker, who was then 14 years old and working in a munitions plant, lacerated her right middle finger when a 25-pound shell dropped on her right hand. She underwent several unsuccessful surgeries to repair tendon damage. Her right hand was permanently impaired, and the Board granted her a permanent disability award in 1946. She returned to work in March 1945 and worked until the munitions plant closed later that year. She did a different job than she did before her injury: she counted shells. After the plant closed, the worker lived with her sister and helped care for her sister's children in exchange for room and board. This arrangement lasted until the worker married. During the course of her marriage, the worker had six children. The worker tried to return to gainful employment to supplement the family income, but she was unsuccessful because of the limitations her impairment imposed. The worker's right hand continued to deteriorate over the years, and she underwent several surgeries. Her right middle finger was amputated, and the Board increased her permanent disability award several times based on deterioration in her condition. The Board granted the worker temporary benefits related to her various surgeries, but it denied her entitlement for further temporary benefits or a pension supplement from 1945 onward.

DecKeywords: Second Injury and Enhancement Fund {SIEF} (severity of preexisting condition)
Suitable employment; Loss of earnings {LOE}; Labour market re-entry {LMR} (eligibility)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a shoulder injury in March 1998. She returned to work, sometimes performing regular work and sometimes modified work. She required several surgeries and could no longer return to pre-accident work. With the final LOE review approaching in May 2004, the Board contacted the employer with a view to securing a position for the worker prior to the review date. The employer provided modified work at no wage loss. The worker had difficulty with the position and laid off. The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution Officer denying LMR services and further LOE benefits.

The employer company, BCH, sought a decision that the portion of payroll classified under Rate Group 764, Classification Unit 4011-009, Homebuilding Operations, should have been transferred to Rate Group 723, Classification Unit 4411-000, Construction Project Management. In the event it was unsuccessful on that issue, the employer requested that all retroactive premium adjustments of the board be rescinded.

DecKeywords: Adjournment (illness of worker); Hearing (attendance of worker)
DecSummary: The employer was appealing a decision of the Board granting the worker entitlement for traumatic mental stress and denying the employer SIEF relief.

A road construction labourer suffered a back injury in July 1999. The worker was laid off in December 1999 as part of a seasonal lay-off, but he was not rehired in the spring of 2000. The Board found that the employer breached its re-employment obligations and assessed the maximum penalty against the employer. However, the Board refused to make payments to the worker equivalent to LOE benefits. The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution Officer denying the payments to the worker.

DecKeywords: Accident (occurrence); Notice of accident (as soon as practicable)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution Officer denying entitlement for an accident.

DecSummary: The worker suffered a back injury in September 2000. She was able to continue working for some time but laid off in February 2001. She returned to modified work in March 2001. On June 18, 2001, the worker began a graduated return to regular work but she stopped working on July 31, 2001. She eventually returned to work with the accident employer at another job in February 2003. The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution Officer denying full LOE benefits from July 31, 2001 to February 2003.

DecKeywords: Procedure (medical examination) (Tribunal assessor) (provision of materials to assessor)
DecSummary: In Decision No. 1692/06I, the Panel decided to obtain a report from a Tribunal medical assessor.

DecSummary: The Board granted the worker entitlement for carpal tunnel syndrome. The employer appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution officer denying SIEF relief.

DecKeywords: Recurrences (compensable injury); Second accident; Earnings basis (recurrences) (FEL)
DecSummary: The worker was granted entitlement for carpal tunnel syndrome in 1990 and for a recurrence in 1995. The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution Officer basing her FEL award on earnings in 1990 rather than in 1995.

DecKeywords: Early and safe return to work {ESRTW} (cooperation)
Suitable employment; Early and safe return to work {ESRTW} (cooperation)
DecSummary: An electrician suffered back, neck and shoulder injuries in a fall in 1999, for which he was granted a 45% NEL award. He returned to modified work at no wage loss as a computer database operator. In 2003, the employer advised that the job as a computer database operator was no longer available. It proposed new modified work as a store room clerk. The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution Officer denying further LOE benefits after 2003.

DecKeywords: Consequences of injury; Continuing entitlement; Permanent impairment {NEL}

DecSummary: The worker suffered a low back injury in August 1999. In December 2002, she was granted a 28% NEL award for organic impairment. In August 2003, she was granted entitlement for chronic pain. In February 2004, the Board replaced the 28% NEL award for organic impairment with a 15% NEL award for chronic pain. The Board commuted the 15% award and paid it as a lump sum. After objection by the worker, in March 2004, the Board overturned the decision granting entitlement for chronic pain, granted entitlement for psychotraumatic disability and reinstated the 28% award.

DecKeywords: Cashier; Disablement (repetitive work); Future economic loss {FEL} (deemed earnings) (employability); Medical report (opinion of treating doctor preferred); Accident (date)
DecSummary: The worker was a cashier at a fruit and vegetable store. At the time of the hearing she was 60 years old. After a decade of performing her cashier job, she began to experience the gradual onset of pain and stiffness in her left shoulder, wrist, and neck. The worker was diagnosed with left shoulder tendonitis and left carpal tunnel syndrome. The Board granted her entitlement for these conditions, but it denied entitlement for problems with her neck and upper back. The Board also set an accident date of July 2, 1996, and granted her a 4% NEL award for her left shoulder and carpal tunnel syndrome in her left wrist. The Board later increased this to 10%. At the worker's initial FEL determination the Board only granted the worker a sustainability award because it found that although she could not continue to work as a cashier, she was capable of performing various other jobs that would restore her pre-accident earnings. The Board confirmed its assessment at the first and final FEL reviews (R1 and R2).

DecKeywords: Second Injury and Enhancement Fund {SIEF} (preexisting condition)
DecSummary: The employer appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution Officer denying the employer entitlement to SIEF relief sought in relation to a claim involving a worker who was granted initial entitlement for bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome related to her duties as an assembler with the employer. The worker was paid for lost time from work from September 10, 2002 to January 2, 2003 and was granted an 8% NEL award for permanent impairment for both wrists following surgery. The employer claimed that the worker's impairment was prolonged due to a pre-existing condition and sought entitlement to SIEF relief. The employer's request was denied on the basis that there was no medical evidence to suggest that the worker had a pre-existing condition in her wrists.

DecKeywords: Earnings basis (minor); Psychotraumatic disability; Pensions (assessment) (disfigurement); Pensions (reassessment)
DecSummary: On August 3, 1989 the worker suffered a fracture of his right femur when he slipped in his employer's parking lot. He underwent surgery related to this injury. At the time of the accident, the worker was 15 years old and employed as a clerk for a grocery store. In December 2003 the Board granted the worker a 3% permanent partial disability award for the residual impairment in his right leg. In April 2005 an ARO denied the worker entitlement for: (1) psychotraumatic disability, (2) a disfigurement award for scarring on the right leg related to the surgery, (3) an increase in the worker's permanent partial disability award, and (4) a recalculation of the permanent partial disability award calculated using a different earnings basis.

DecKeywords: Correctional officer (young offenders); Harassment (sex); Stress, mental
DecSummary: The worker was a residential youth worker at a maximum security residential facility for young offenders. The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution Officer denying entitlement for stress-related disability.

DecKeywords: Chronic pain (consistency with organic findings); Psychotraumatic disability
Disablement (repetitive work); Osteoarthritis (knee); Hospital employment (housekeeping aide)
DecSummary: A 53-year-old housekeeping aide at a hospital did not have entitlement for osteoarthritis of her knees. The condition was not a disablement from the nature of her work. Her work duties were varied. Osteoarthritis is extremely common in the population for people in their fifth and sixth decades. The worker may have had to stop working because of her osteoarthritis but the work duties were not the cause of the condition.

DecSummary: The worker suffered a whiplash-type injury in 1983, for which he was granted a 20% pension, later increased to 30%. DecKeywords: Procedure (reconsideration) (Tribunal initiative); Reconsideration (error of law); Evidence (confidential information) (health profession proceedings)
DecSummary: In Decision No. 167/06, a vice-chair found that the worker did not have entitlement for chronic pain. In the decision, the vice-chair gave weight to a letter from a doctor addressed to the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario. The letter was sent in response to a complaint filed by the worker's representative. The complaint alleged that the doctor had not responded to requests to provide information to the Board. The doctor's letter, a copy of which was sent to the Board, was intemperate and made assertions that were harmful to the worker's claim.

DecKeywords: Psychotraumatic disability; Stress, mental; Time limits (appeal) (date of Board decision); Harassment
DecSummary: The Board granted the worker entitlement for carpal tunnel syndrome in November 1999. When the worker returned to work following surgery, he was harassed by co-workers who put a box on his head with a sign on it asking for donations for carpal tunnel. The worker's estate appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution Officer denying entitlement for psychotraumatic disability or stress-related disability. The employer appealed denial of an extension of the time to appeal initial entitlement for carpal tunnel syndrome.

DecKeywords: Time limits (appeal) (diligence of applicant) (personal matters); Time limits (appeal) (unrepresented worker)

The worker was prepared to clean the lunchroom but claimed that he could not clean the bathroom because of a gastric condition which caused him to become nauseous from bathroom smells. He subsequently provided medical evidence confirming the gastric condition. When the worker refused to do the bathroom cleaning, the employer sent the worker home. He was off work for three days.

DecKeywords: Time limits (appeal) (diligence of applicant) (personal matters); Time limits (appeal) (intent) (notice to Board)

DecSummary: The worker's application to extend the time to appeal was denied. The worker had previously withdrawn the appeal on the issue in question. In the decision allowing the withdrawal, it was clearly stated that any future appeal would be subject to the time limits. The worker was not diligent in seeking to reinstate the appeal.

DecSummary: The worker suffered a back injury in 1969, for which he was granted a 10% pension, later increased to 20%, then to 35%, then to 40% and finally to 60%. The Board also granted entitlement for erectile dysfunction and a neurogenic bladder condition resulting from back surgery in 1993. The Board granted a 5% pension for the bladder condition and 2% pension for the erectile dysfunction. The worker appealed, claiming that he was entitled to a 100% pension.

DecSummary: A Board Claims Adjudicator granted the worker entitlement for a back injury in July 1999 on an aggravation basis, and paid LOE benefits until July 1999. The worker appealed to the Appeals Resolution Officer, claiming entitlement to ongoing benefits. The worker apparently claimed the his herniated disc was caused by the accident and argued in the alternative that he had entitlement on an aggravation basis. The ARO considered the issue of initial entitlement to be before her, and concluded that the worker did not have entitlement for the accident at all. The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution Officer.

The worker suffered a laceration to his heel in 1990. The injury did not heal as anticipated, and he experienced recurrent swelling and infections. He underwent four surgeries. He was granted a 2% NEL award, later increased to 13% and then to 15%. The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution Officer denying reimbursement for the cost of marijuana used for pain relief, denying a NEL award for disfigurement and denying reassessment of the NEL award to include toe, knee and hip conditions.

The employer's application to extend the time to appeal was granted. The employer had originally filed notice of appeal within the time limit, but withdrew the appeal. The employer then asked to reinstate the appeal after only one month promptly after realizing that the employer was still liable for the costs of the claim under the employer's experience rating plan.
The worker was entitled to a full FEL award. Her decision to decline substance abuse treatment was academic in the circumstances, because the worker was competitively unemployable in any event.

DecKeywords: Earnings basis (average weekly earnings); Earnings basis (period of unemployment); Earnings basis (seasonal employment)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a left hand injury in October 1996. She returned to modified work at no wage loss in May 1997. She was permanently laid off in March 2001 due to a plant relocation. The Board originally based benefits on the worker's earnings at the time of the accident in accordance with s. 40(1)(a) of the pre-1997 Act. On application by the employer, the Board calculated benefits under s. 40(1)(b), resulting in a reduction of the worker's earnings basis from $330 per week to $208 per week. The worker appealed.

DecKeywords: Board Directives and Guidelines (hearing loss) (individual susceptibility); Hearing loss
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution Officer denying entitlement for hearing loss.

DecKeywords: Suitable employment; Exposure (chemicals); Board Directives and Guidelines (suitable employment) (health and safety risks)
DecSummary: A worker at a chemical plant developed a sensitivity to trimellitic anhydride in January 2002. The Board granted entitlement and a 5% NEL award. The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution Officer denying LOE benefits after April 2002.

DecKeywords: Cancer (lung) (squamous cell); Smoking; Mining (nickel); Significant contribution (of employment to occupational disease)
DecSummary: On November 22, 1999 the worker was diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the right lower lobe of the lung. The worker's union, on behalf of the worker, wrote to the Board on December 1, 1999 to request entitlement for lung cancer as a result of his employment as a Blacksmith and Maintenance Mechanic in a nickel mine. The worker died on December 6, 1999. The Board denied the claim, and the worker's estate appealed to the Tribunal.

DecKeywords: Consequences of injury; Fibromyalgia; Supplements, transitional provisions (permanent)

DecSummary: The Panel clarified Decision No. 1777/06 by stating that the 2003 claim should be treated as a recurrence of the 1985 injury. However, the Panel would not direct that the Board manually adjust the employer's NEER account. The employer could pursue that matter at the Board.
The worker's estate appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution Officer denying the worker entitlement for lung cancer related to his work for a nickel company from 1952 to 1984.

The worker worked for a nickel producer for 38 years from 1959 to 1997. In 2000, he was diagnosed with colon cancer. The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution Officer denying entitlement.

The employer appealed the ARO's decision that found the worker was entitled to benefits under the Board's Traumatic Mental Stress policy. The employer contended that the worker embellished the extent of his psychotraumatic disability and that even if he did not, he was not entitled to LOE benefits during the period of seasonal lay-off.

DecKeywords: Respiratory condition; Transportation industry (bus driver); Exposure (mould)
DecSummary: A bus driver appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution Officer denying entitlement for a respiratory condition, which the worker related to exposure to mould on the buses that he drove.

DecKeywords: Election; In the course of employment (parking lots); Right to sue
DecSummary: The plaintiff in a civil case parked in the parking lot leased and maintained by his employer. As he was walking through the parking lot to the plant prior to start of his shift, he was struck by a vehicle driven by an employee of the security company hired by the employer to patrol the parking lot. The plaintiff brought an action against the driver of the vehicle and the owner of the vehicle. The defendants applied to determine whether the plaintiff's right of action was taken away.
The worker's application to reconsider Decision No. 1582/06 was denied. The worker was essentially trying to re-argue the case.

The worker's application to reconsider Decision No. 1190/06 was denied. The original hearing was conducted by way of written submissions. While the Tribunal is required to provide parties with an opportunity for a hearing, there is not requirement that the hearing must be an oral hearing. The Vice-Chair also noted that the worker had consented proceeding by way of written submissions.

The worker suffered a back injury in 1979. In 2004, he was granted a 20% pension retroactive to 2003. The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution Officer confirming the amount of the pension and the arrears.

DecKeywords: Earnings basis (deemed worker); Personal coverage (actual earnings); Permanent impairment {NEL} (degree of impairment) (heart condition)
DecSummary: A self-employed worker with personal coverage suffered a heart attack in May 1993. In Decision No. 1556/04, the Tribunal concluded that the worker had entitlement for the heart attack. The Board then based benefits on earnings of $17,000 per year and granted a 55% NEL award. The worker appealed.
In Decision No. 1013/04, the Tribunal allowed the employer's appeal and found that the accident date for the worker's dermatitis claim should be in 1989 rather than in 2000.

DecKeywords: Aggravation (preexisting condition); Continuing entitlement; Board Directives and Guidelines (aggravation) (preexisting condition)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a back injury in October 2003. The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution Officer denying LOE benefits after April 2004.
The original hearing Panel clarified Decision No. 1340/06 after apparent misunderstanding by the Board in implementing the decision.

DecKeywords: Availability for employment (job search); Loss of earnings {LOE} (level of benefits)
Construction (drywall installer); Earnings basis (long-term); Board Directives and Guidelines (earnings basis) (non-permanent or irregular employment)
DecSummary: A drywall taper suffered a low back injury in October 2001. Short-term benefits were based on the worker's report of earning $25 per hour, with no deductions. The Board based long-term benefits on net earnings reported in the worker's income tax returns for the two years prior to the accident. The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution Officer confirming the long-term earnings basis.

DecSummary: A flagman at a construction site had entitlement for plantar fasciitis. The condition was a disablement from continuous standing. However, the entitlement was for aggravation of a pre-existing degenerative condition. The worker was not entitled to a NEL award for permanent impairment.

On March 8, 1999 the worker, a plumber, sustained an injury to his neck. His family physician diagnosed a cervical strain. On August 22, 2002 the worker was again injured at work. He was laid off on November 15, 2002 for reasons unrelated to his injury. He sought entitlement to benefits subsequent to that date on the ground that he had a continuing disability that affected his ability to work. The ARO decision denied entitlement and implied that any ongoing symptoms after November 15, 2002 were related to non-compensable underlying degenerative changes, not to the injury of 2002.
The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution Officer denying entitlement for a hernia.

DecSummary: On approximately February 15, 2002 the worker, a mechanic, experienced an onset of pain in his back while replacing a leaf spring on a logging trailer. He was diagnosed with sacroiliac strain. The Board granted the worker LOE benefits beginning February 25, 2002. The accident employer offered modified work that was to begin on January 2, 2003. The worker did not appear for this work. The Board terminated the worker's LOE benefits as of January 2, 2003 because he refused suitable modified work. The employer sought SIEF relief for the costs of the worker's claim and claimed that the worker should not have been entitled to LOE benefits from April 2002 to January 2003.

DecKeywords: Hearing loss (deterioration after removal from exposure)
Accident (definition of); Arising out of employment (common activity); Chance event; Injury by accident
DecSummary: The worker was going down stairs, realized that he had forgotten something, turned around and began to lift his leg to go back up the stairs, when he felt an immediate onset of pain in his leg. The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution Officer denying entitlement.

DecSummary: The Board sent the worker to Toronto for a medical appointment. The appointment was scheduled during a cycle in the worker's shift when he was not scheduled to work. The employer's application to reconsider Decision No. 1071/06R4 was denied. There was no fundamental error of law or process in the Decision No. 1071/06R4. The employer was essentially trying to re-argue the case.
The worker applied for reconsideration of Decision No. 2102/06.

In Decision No. 556/06 (released in June 2008), the hearing panel found that the worker was entitled to a full FEL award from R1 in June 2003, until she reaches age 65 in July 2042. The Board applied for reconsideration of Decision No. 556/06.

In Decision No. 2190/06, the Vice-Chair found that the worker had entitlement for fibromyalgia. In accordance with Decision No. 2190/06R2, the Vice-Chair now reheard the worker's appeal regarding entitlement to LOE benefits from 2003 to 2006, and concluded that the worker was entitled to partial LOE benefits based on ability to work part-time at minimum wage.

In Decision No. 1071/06R3, the Vice-Chair found that the worker was engaged in fraud or misrepresentation regarding his claim for psychotraumatic disability prior to the R2 FEL review date, thus allowing review of the worker's FEL award. The Vice-Chair then found that the worker was capable of working full-time in the identified SEB.
The worker's application for reconsideration of Decision No. 1062/06 was denied. The worker was essentially trying to re-argue the case.
The worker's estate appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution Officer denying the worker entitlement for lung cancer.

DecSummary: The worker suffered a low back injury in 1992, for which the Board granted the worker a 22% NEL award, later increased to 33%. The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Resolution Officer denying entitlement for chronic pain disability or psychotraumatic disability.

DecSummary: The worker suffered a back injury in 1994. The Board denied ongoing benefits after June 1995 and denied entitlement for chronic pain disability. In Decision No. 373/06, the Tribunal found that there was no compensable basis for the worker's back problems beyond June 1995 on either an organic basis or non-organic basis.

The worker's application for reconsideration of Decision No. 574/06 was denied. The worker submitted a new x-ray report. However, the Vice-Chair found that the x-ray, by itself, without any medical opinion explaining the relevance of the findings when compared to observations during a medical examination or to the circumstances of the appeal, was not significant evidence.

DecSummary: The worker applied for reconsideration of Decision No. 101/06, in which the hearing panel denied the worker entitlement for post-traumatic stress disorder.

DecKeywords: Chronic pain; Reconsideration (error of law); Reconsideration (administrative error)
DecSummary: This reconsideration request did not show that there was any fundamental error of law or process in the original decision, nor did the worker raise significant new evidence that would not have been available at the time of the hearing. In addition, the worker had not shown any significant defect in the original decision. Accordingly, the Vice-Chair concluded that the threshold test for granting a reconsideration request was not met.
